Valid lower bound: 14 insufficient because 13 same-type draws from mixed vs 13 from pure are indistinguishable. Proper worst-case reasoning.

summary: Only response_C correctly solves the puzzle with answer 15, valid concrete strategy (1 from 'Mixed' label + up to 14 from uncertain envelope), proper upper bound proof (14 identical observations proves purity since mixed has max 13), and valid lower bound (14 draws insufficient as 13 same-type draws from pure vs mixed are indistinguishable). All other solutions fail on fundamental aspects: wrong final numbers, invalid one-draw-inference claims, missing worst-case analysis, or contradictory answers. The key insight is that since the mixed envelope contains at most 13 of any single type, 14 observations of the same type proves purity, making 1+14=15 the minimum.
